text: dsh-browser-tab 是 DSH Web GUI 的会话管理插件，在 shell.overlay 挂载会话标签栏、收藏抽屉和最近关闭抽屉。它记录当前浏览器中打开过的会话，点击标签切换会话，并可关闭标签、拖动排序、标记收藏及按文件夹整理收藏；手动关闭的会话可从最近关闭列表重新打开。适合希望在 DSH 网页端并排管理多个会话的用户。标签、收藏和关闭记录保存在浏览器 localStorage 中。

dsh-browser-tab adds a session tab strip, favorites drawer, and recently closed drawer to the DSH Web GUI. Users can switch, close, and reorder session tabs, organize bookmarks into folders, and reopen manually closed sessions. It stores these records in the current browser’s localStorage.
想在 DSH 网页里用标签切换最近打开的会话
I want browser-like tabs to switch between my DSH web sessions.
Can I bookmark DSH sessions and organize them into folders?
dsh-browser-tab 的功能「会话标签栏」：自动记录当前会话并显示为可切换标签；点击其他标签切换会话，也可关闭或拖动调整顺序。
dsh-browser-tab 的功能「收藏与最近关闭」：通过标签操作收藏会话并在抽屉中用文件夹管理；关闭标签会记入最近关闭列表，可从列表重新打开仍存在的会话。

dsh-browser-tab README · dsh-browser-tab：A recent-session tab strip for the DSH Web GUI, shaped like browser tabs: every
session you open adds a tab, clicking a tab switches to that session, and a tab
disappears only when you close it. Favorites are a drawer dropping from the right
end of that strip, the way a browser keeps its bookmarks — and like a browser,
open tabs and bookmarks are two separate lists: closing a tab never removes its
bookmark. The tabs you close by hand are remembered too: a short `Recently
closed` list sits next to the favorites button, so a tab closed by mistake is
one click away from being reopened.

dsh-browser-tab README · Behaviour：- **Hover to reveal.** The strip is parked off-screen at the top edge. Move the
  pointer into the top 10px band and it slides down; move away and it retracts
  after 260ms. It never covers the conversation while you are reading.
- **Wide and centred.** The strip spans 90% of the viewport width, centred on
  the top edge, so a wide screen shows more tabs instead of the same narrow
  column; the tab row scrolls inside it when they still do not fit.
- **Wheel scrolls the tabs.** With the pointer over the tab row, the wheel moves
  the tabs sideways instead of the page — one notch of vertical wheel travels a
  stretch of horizontal row, with no Shift needed, like a browser's tab bar. The
  movement is not animated, and it only applies over the row itself: over the
  favorites button or outside the strip the wheel is left alone.
- **Automatic collection.** Opening a session (from the sidebar, a link, or a
  fresh session) adds its tab, in first-seen order.
- **Click to switch.** The current session's tab carries a green dot; clicking
  any other tab selects that session.

dsh-browser-tab README · Placement：Three additive registrations, none of them replacing a shipped entry:

| Slot | Surface |
| --- | --- |
| `shell.overlay` | The tab strip, above every column and outside their scroll containers. It also renders the `Recently closed` and `Favorites` buttons at its own right end. |
| `shell.overlay` | The favorites drawer, a sibling of the strip in the same list slot. |
| `shell.overlay` | The recently-closed drawer, a third sibling in that slot. |

dsh-browser-tab README · Placement：The buttons are part of the strip rather than registrations of their own: they
belong to that one row, at its right end and outside the scrolling tab row, and
keeping them there means each drawer hangs off the strip's corner. Nothing is
added to the session header, so no shipped header seat is shadowed. Each
registration is wrapped in its own `try`/`catch` — a failed mount degrades one
surface, it never takes the shell down.

dsh-browser-tab README · Placement：Each drawer and its button are separate mounts, so the open flags live in
`fav-drawer-state.ts` and `hist-drawer-state.ts`, module-level observables that
are never persisted. The strip subscribes to both: an open drawer pins the strip
on screen, since a parked strip would put that drawer's anchor above the
viewport.

dsh-browser-tab README · Architecture：| Half | File | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host | `src/index.ts` | No-op. The feature is entirely client-side. |
| Client | `src/client/index.ts` | Registers the dictionaries and mounts the three surfaces (strip, favorites drawer, closed-history drawer), each in its own `try`/`catch`. |
| Client | `src/client/RecentTabs.tsx` | The React strip: one row of tabs, the two tail triggers, hover and drag state, inline rename, and the per-tab context menu. It also holds the strip on screen while either drawer is open. |

| Client | `src/client/FavoritesPanel.tsx` | The favorites drawer: anchors itself to the trigger rectangle, pins the current session, draws the bookmark tree, creates and renames folders, drags rows vertically and files them into folders. |

dsh-browser-tab README · Architecture：Session data comes from the Session Controller's `ctx.sessions.list` snapshot
source plus `ctx.uiWorkspace.openSession(id)`. The surfaces are global while
Slot props are session-scoped, so they deliberately do not read `useSessions`
from props.

The stored list is authoritative for *membership*; the live session list is
authoritative for *titles and presence*. That split is what lets a retained tab
outlive its session without losing its last known name.

dsh-browser-tab README · Architecture：Favorites are a collection of their own, not a flag on a stored row. They form a
tree: `favorites` is its top level, and a folder is a node that holds bookmark
rows and other folders. `toggleFavorite` pins a session at the top level and
unpins it wherever it sits, `moveFavorite` reorders siblings inside their own
layer, and the folder operations (`createFolder`, `renameFolder`,
`removeFolder`, `moveFavoriteInto`, `moveFolderInto`) only ever rewrite that
tree. None of them touches the tab list or the activation order, which is what
lets closing a tab leave its bookmark in place.

dsh-browser-tab README · Architecture：The closed history is the third collection, and it records an event rather than
a membership: `controller.remove` is its only writer, so a session that merely
left the live list never lands there. `recordTab` takes an id back out of it, so
the strip and the history never list the same session at once, and
`recordClosed` keeps the list to `MAX_CLOSED` rows, newest first.

dsh-browser-tab README · Architecture：The context menu is drawn by this plugin, not by a shell menu component: it is
a `position: fixed` popup at the click point, clamped into the viewport, and it
carries no shell class names.

dsh-browser-tab README · Rapid switching：Recording a session is idempotent: `recordTab` and the controller both return
the same snapshot reference when an observation changes nothing, and they notify
subscribers only for a real change. Clicking back and forth between two tabs
therefore cannot re-enter the render loop, which is what produced the earlier
flicker when the strip was a dynamic plugin.

dsh-browser-tab README · Install：From npm, or from any plugin market that indexes it:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-browser-tab
```

Or from a checkout, as a local bundle:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:<repo>/my-plugins/dsh-browser-tab
```

Then restart the profile so the Host half registers.

dsh-browser-tab README · Local checks：```sh
pnpm --filter dsh-browser-tab typecheck
pnpm --filter dsh-browser-tab test
pnpm --filter dsh-browser-tab build
```

dsh-browser-tab README · Limits：- The strip lists sessions opened **in this browser**. Another browser, another
  profile, or a private window has its own list.
- Storage is best-effort: if the browser blocks `localStorage` (private mode in
  some configurations, or a quota fault), the strip still works for the current
  page lifetime but does not persist.
- The list is capped at 40 tabs; older entries are dropped as new ones arrive.
- The recently-closed history keeps the last 10 closes; older ones fall off, and
  it lives in this browser's storage like the rest of the record.
